# Carelink Psykiatri Viborg

Carelink Psykiatri Viborg is a private mental health provider (also referred to in the source material as "Carelink psykiatri, Nærhospital Viborg" [^src7]) that appears repeatedly in Denmark's ADHD database annual report as one of the private actors treating patients with ADHD alongside the public regional psychiatric system. Its main claim to significance is a strikingly low score on Indicator 4, the measure of coordinating network meetings held within 90 days of treatment start for children and young people under 18: the clinic reported meeting this standard in only 1 % of cases, the lowest rate among the private providers discussed in the report, compared with 5 % at Carelink Psykiatri Kolding [^src1].

Beyond this headline figure, the clinic's performance varies sharply across the different quality indicators tracked in the ADHD database for the reporting period 01.04.2024–31.03.2025. On one measure it recorded zero out of 118 relevant cases (0 %, confidence interval 0–3) [^src2], while on another — concerning medication use — it scored 102 out of 118 cases, or 86 % (confidence interval 79–92) [^src3]. This 86 % figure places Carelink Psykiatri Viborg within the broader finding that private hospitals' patients are medicated for ADHD at rates between 86 % and 100 % [^src3], a notably higher share than in the public system. Elsewhere the clinic shows very small denominators and wide uncertainty: 0 out of 3 cases (0 %, confidence interval 0–71) on one indicator [^src4], 0 out of 6 cases (0 %, confidence interval 0–46) on another [^src5], and 5 out of 6 cases (83 %, confidence interval 36–100) on a further measure [^src6].

These figures sit within a broader national picture described in the ADHD database's context for Indicator 4: the country-wide fulfilment rate for coordinating network meetings has remained stable but far below the 90 % development target, averaging just 20 % nationally. The database's steering group has pointed to pressure on both specialised psychiatry and primary care, geographic barriers, and competing priorities as explanations, and has since revised the indicator to instead track contact with a patient's home municipality within 120 days of the start of diagnostic assessment. Carelink Psykiatri Viborg's 1 % score places it at the very bottom of this already low-performing national landscape [^src1]. No relationships involving other named individuals or organizations (beyond fellow private providers Carelink Psykiatri Kolding and Carelink Psykiatri Roskilde, mentioned in shared statistics) are documented in the source material.
